newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ING says life insurance competition hots up.
newsitem.headline: ING says life insurance competition hots up.

text.p: Nationale-Nederlanden, unit of financial services group ING, said on Thursday it expected more players in the already overcrowded Dutch life insurance market, but it remained upbeat on its own market share.

Nationale-Nederlanden increased its market share in the Dutch life insurance market to 22 percent in 1995 from 21.7 percent in 1994 and it said data on its 1996 market share would be available later this year.
"We are hopeful for 1996," said chairman Durk Brands of Nationale-Nederlanden, who is also member of the board of ING.
Brands said that the Dutch life insurance market was still very lucrative, although many new players were expected to enter the market which would make competition even tougher.
"I do not expect less interest for the Dutch life insurance market," said Brands, after announcing the group's 1996 results.
Nationale-Nederland posted a 12 percent higher 1996 net profit of 802 million guilders.
The net result from its life insurance activities rose to 648 million guilders in 1996 from 565 million guilders in 1995.
Gross premium income from life activities increased to 6,506 million in 1996 from 6,220 in 1995.
Earlier this month, parent company ING reported its total 1996 net profit had risen to 3.32 billion guilders from 2.65 billion in 1995.
